analysis:
All changes in this batch are test-only: the GLM5Next fixture, GlobalKVCacheBudgetProcessTests, SystemMemoryAdmissionTests and SystemMemoryTests. No production code, wire protocol, attestation, authorization or key-handling logic is touched.

GLM5NextProtectedFactoryFixture.swift (lines 111-112) adds the `<think>` and `</think>` atomic tokens to the synthetic tokenizer vocabulary so the serving tokenizer accepts the fixture. It uses synthetic weights and a per-test temp root under SSDTestDirectory. Cache environment is test-scoped: DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT, an ephemeral key, and the kv-backend-guard path redirected into the fixture root. This does not touch live A-003/T-041 artifacts or the real KEK.

The memory tests switch the SystemMemory.availableBytes call from (freePages, inactivePages) to a `stats: vm_statistics64` signature, built with the new machVMStatistics helper. Renamed tests (inactive to reclaim credit) show the free-only policy now treats file-backed/external pages as reclaimable credit that free-only must not spend. This implies a production SystemMemory.availableBytes signature and semantics change, which is not in the supplied units. It relates to availability and memory admission (T-010/T-029-class DoS) rather than confidentiality. The tests still assert that the free-only policy rejects shared-host credit, so the guard is preserved.

The visible SystemMemoryTests.swift patch is truncated and has no head text. Cross-file check not possible here: the production availableBytes implementation, and whether the reclaimable policy's computation from external_page_count and purgeable counts could over-admit loads. The next pass should check that production file if it is in the PR. No security regression is identified in the supplied test code. Remaining uncertainty is the unseen production memory-sampling change.
